title: Saying no with an alternative: the art of refusing well

videos.script: Seventeen days before Black Friday, the CEO asks the checkout team for flash deals. A countdown, a deep discount, stock reserved for whoever gets there first. {{title}} Everybody looks at the tech lead, and the tech lead looks at Lívia. {{capacity}} Saying yes in the corridor feels like loyalty. It also puts eighty-five days of work into sixty, in the month when an outage costs the most. A vague yes is worse. The team cannot keep it, and everybody finds out on the day. {{vague}} This lesson is about the other answer. A no in five parts: the need, the no, the reason, an alternative, and what would change it. {{five}} Then saying it to your own boss, and in writing, where every softening word is permanent.
